issue.title: FISH+: help to support your system (please run one probe script)
issue.author: unxed
issue.body:
f4 is getting **FISH+**, a file system over a plain SSH shell — no SFTP server, no agent on the far side, just the shell and whatever utilities are already installed there. Which utilities are available differs wildly between systems, and we can only test the ones we own.

If you have shell access to anything that is **not** mainstream GNU/Linux — macOS, FreeBSD/OpenBSD/NetBSD, Solaris/illumos, AIX, BusyBox or Alpine, an OpenWrt router, a NAS, Android/Termux, WSL, a Docker image with a minimal userland, an ancient box with an ancient shell — please help:

1. Grab `tools/fishplus_probe.sh` from the repository.
2. Run it **on that machine**: `sh fishplus_probe.sh 2>&1 | tee fishplus-probe.txt`
3. Post the output here, together with one line saying what the system is.

The script only reads: it creates nothing, changes nothing, removes nothing, and touches no file outside the current directory. Please look through the output before posting — it contains a listing of the current directory and of `/`, so run it somewhere you do not mind sharing.

What we are trying to learn: whether `find -printf`, GNU `stat -c` or BSD `stat -f` works and in what exact format; what `ls -l` looks like there (this becomes the last-resort listing backend); whether `dd`, `head -c` and `base64` behave the way we need for reading and writing files; how the shell's `read` builtin treats a line.

Results feed directly into `plugins/netfox/fishplus/helper.sh`, and every system reported here gets a parser and a place in the test suite. Thanks!
